question.text: Will a division (bloc vote) be held on Malaysia's Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat on 26 November 2026?
question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves YES if, between 00:00 UTC and 20:00 UTC on 26 November 2026 (08:00 MYT on 26 November to 04:00 MYT on 27 November 2026), the Dewan Rakyat (Malaysia's House of Representatives) holds at least one division ("belah bahagi" — a recorded vote in which the ayes and noes are counted) on the Supply Bill 2027 (Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 / Rang Undang-Undang Perbekalan 2027), whether on a committee-stage allocation or on the bill's third reading. It resolves NO if no such division is held within that period, including if the House rises without any division being called on the bill. Resolution is based on the official Dewan Rakyat Hansard (Penyata Rasmi) for that sitting; if that record is unavailable, [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) reporting the proceedings will be used.
question.fine_print: A division counts only if it concerns the Supply Bill 2027 — including a proposed reduction of a ministry's or department's allocation at committee stage, or the third reading itself; divisions on unrelated business do not count. Where a division's timing could fall outside the window, only divisions recorded before 20:00 UTC on 26 November 2026 count.

research:
I found no division on the Supply Bill 2027 so far, and no reporting of a plan to call one on 26 November. In the past four Anwar-era budget cycles (and in 2021 under Ismail Sabri), the final stage passed by voice vote. The one division under Anwar came at the Budget 2026 policy stage.

## 1. Resolution source
- The deciding record is the Dewan Rakyat Hansard (Penyata Rasmi) for 26 Nov 2026, which does not exist yet. I did not try to read raw data from parlimen.gov.my and found no order paper for 26 Nov. If the Hansard is unavailable, news reports of the sitting will be used.
- 2026-11-13: Committee-stage debate runs until 26 Nov, with 16 ministries still to wind up. That article does not explicitly confirm the third reading for 26 Nov. It reports the bill's committee-stage approvals so far as voice votes and mentions no bloc votes. [Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2026/11/13/no-gst-anwar-reaffirms-stance-as-dewan-rakyat-ends-sixth-week-with-deficit-cut-to-37pc/243083)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question. I found no report of any division on Supply Bill 2027 since committee stage began on 2 Nov.
- 2026-11-04: The Economy Ministry's allocation was approved "with a majority vote", with no division reported. [Bernama](https://www.bernama.com/en/general/news.php?id=2630079)
- 2026-10-29: The policy stage passed by voice vote, and no opposition MP called for a division. [FMT](https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2026/10/29/dewan-rakyat-passes-2027-supply-bill-at-policy-stage); [Malaysiakini](https://www.malaysiakini.com/news/888129-budget-2027-breezes-through-dewan-rakyat-after-csa-signing)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-16: There was a row over Deputy Speaker Ramli Mohd Nor leaving the chair to join the Works Ministry committee debate, and criticism came from both sides. [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2026/11/16/rare-scene-in-dewan-rakyat-as-deputy-speaker-steps-down-from-chair-to-join-budget-debate); [Malaysiakini](https://www.malaysiakini.com/news/889208-insult-of-parliament-deputy-speaker-sparks-bipartisan-backlash-by-debating-budget-while-presiding)
- 2026-11-16: Committee debate continued, including Works Ministry (Wee Jeck Seng). Finance Bill 2026 was tabled for first reading. [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2026/11/16/make-federal-road-ft005-a-priority-wee-says)
- 2026-11-15: A senator warned that dissolving Parliament early would derail Budget 2027. [Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2026/11/15/senator-warns-early-parliament-dissolution-could-derail-budget-2027-and-force-temporary-spending-citing-2022-precedent/243405)
- 2026-10: Opposition Leader Hamzah Zainudin attended the CSA signing but did not sign. He reportedly said it was too soon to say whether the opposition would back the budget, and he called it "lacking vision". PAS, with 43 MPs, is now the opposition's core, which is more than enough for the 15 MPs needed to back a division call. [NST](https://www.nst.com.my/amp/news/nation/2026/10/1566204/zahid-hamzah-among-those-mou-signing-ceremony-parliament); [Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2026/10/15/pushing-mega-projects-hamzah-zainudin-criticises-budget-2027-as-lacking-vision/239217); [FMT](https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2026/10/15/pas-need-not-hold-opposition-leader-post-says-treasurer)
- I found no statement from PN or PAS about calling a division at the third reading.

## 4. Base rates
- 2025-12-01: The Budget 2026 third reading passed by voice vote. The only division that cycle was at the policy stage on 4 Nov 2025 (120-67). [Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2025/12/01/anwars-budget-2026-sails-through-dewan-rakyat-with-majority-support/200400); [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2025/12/01/dewan-rakyat-passes-budget-2026)
- 2025-11-11: Three ministries' Budget 2026 allocations were approved by voice vote. [Malay Mail](https://malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2025/11/11/budget-2026-allocations-for-three-ministries-approved-in-dewan-rakyat-via-voice-vote/197934)
- 2024-12-03: Budget 2025 passed by voice vote. [FMT](https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/nation/2024/12/03/budget-2025-passed-in-dewan-rakyat)
- 2023-11-27: Budget 2024 passed by voice vote. [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2023/11/28/budget-2024-passed-with-voice-vote)
- 2021-12-13: Budget 2022 passed by voice vote while a government-opposition MoU was in force. A division call by Warisan at the policy stage did not succeed. [The Star](https://www.thestar.com.my/news/nation/2021/12/14/budget-2022-passed-through-voice-vote); [TMI](https://www.themalaysianinsight.com/s/351880)
- 2020-12: Budget 2021 is the exception. With a thin majority, there were 7 committee-stage divisions and a third-reading division (111-108). [Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2020/12/15/much-ado-in-parliament-but-perikatans-budget-2021-clears-third-reading-by-t/1932137); [Yahoo/Malay Mail](https://malaysia.news.yahoo.com/allocations-three-ministries-approved-opposition-071750066.html)
- Pattern: no final-day division in any of the last four budget cycles (2021 to 2024 sittings, i.e. Budgets 2022 and 2024-2026). I did not check Budget 2023 (passed March 2023). Divisions have mostly come when the government's majority was contested.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no market on this question on Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold or Metaculus.
- Related markets (fetched 2026-11-16):
  - Polymarket gives Malaysia's parliament being dissolved by 31 Dec 2026 a 0.7% chance.
  - Polymarket gives Anwar leaving office by 31 Dec 2026 an 8.5% chance.
  - Kalshi's market on who wins Malaysia's next general election in 2027 has BN at 0.59, PH at 0.28 and PN at 0.17.
  - None of these bear directly on a division.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 16-19 and 23-26 Nov: the remaining committee-stage sittings. The opposition could call a division on a proposed cut to a ministry's allocation, but only one on 26 Nov counts.
- 26 Nov: the final committee-stage winding-ups and the expected third reading. Watch for:
  - PN or PAS whip signals, especially whether Takiyuddin repeats his 2025 tactic of forcing a division.
  - Fallout from the 14 Nov Melaka election and the UMNO-DAP friction.
  - Whether the sitting runs past the 04:00 MYT cutoff on 27 Nov.
- 30 Nov: the Dewan Negara debate begins, which confirms the Dewan Rakyat has to finish by then.

**Bottom line:** I found no division (bloc vote) on the Supply Bill 2027 at any stage so far. Under the Anwar government, every budget's committee stage and third reading since 2023 appears to have passed by voice vote. The one recorded division I found was at the policy stage of Budget 2026. Two further risks: past third readings have sometimes slipped past the scheduled committee-stage end date, and I found no confirmed timetable showing the third reading on 26 November.

The opposition forced several committee-stage divisions, for example Finance Ministry 107-95 and MITI passing by six votes. One attempt failed because only 13 MPs stood, short of the 15 needed. - Taken together, from 2023 to 2025 I found 0 of 3 Anwar-era budgets with a division at the committee stage or the third reading. I could not search every committee-stage day exhaustively.

A slipped timetable could push the third reading past 26 November, as happened in 2025. [Malay Mail](https://www.malaymail.com/news/malaysia/2026/11/13/no-gst-anwar-reaffirms-stance-as-dewan-rakyat-ends-sixth-week-with-deficit-cut-to-37pc/243083)

- Background risks: UMNO-DAP friction, fallout from the Melaka election, and dissolution speculation. Markets put dissolution before year end very low.

forecasts.reasoning:
(a) About 10 days remain: the outcome is known after the 26 November sitting (cutoff 20:00 UTC, 04:00 MYT on 27 November). For Yes, at least 15 MPs must back a call for a recorded division (belah bahagi) on the Supply Bill 2027 during that window. The division could be on a committee-stage allocation or on the third reading, and it must happen that day.

(b) The status quo is No. Every Supply Bill 2027 vote so far has been by voice: the policy stage on 29 October and all committee allocations reported. No opposition plan to force a division has been reported.

(c) Base rate: in the Anwar-era budget cycles (Budgets 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026), none had a division at committee stage or third reading. Budget 2022, under the MoU, also passed its final stage by voice vote. The only recent final-stage divisions came in 2020, under a government with a contested, razor-thin majority. Over this reference class, the final-day division rate is roughly 0 of 5. With smoothing, that gives about 5-10%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- Perikatan Nasional (PN) refused the confidence and supply agreement (CSA), and its leaders dispute Muhyiddin's deal. Putting the 13 signatories on record could be politically attractive.
- PN forced a division at the Budget 2026 policy stage (4 November 2025).
- PAS has 43 MPs, well above the 15 needed to back a division call.
- The Melaka election (14 November) and UMNO-DAP friction add political heat.

Evidence for No:
- No division was called at the 2027 policy stage on 29 October 2026, the most salient moment, just hours after the CSA signing.
- All committee approvals so far have been voice votes (4, 13 and 16 November reporting).
- No PN or PAS statement signals a division plan.
- The Budget 2026 third reading slipped from the scheduled 27 November to 1 December 2025. A similar slip this year would move the third reading outside the window.

(e) No scenario: the final ministries wind up on 26 November, the Speaker calls the voice votes, and PN registers objection orally without standing for a division. Alternatively, the third reading slips to 1 December.

Yes scenario: after the Melaka result and an internal PN feud, Takiyuddin calls for a division on the third reading so that the CSA signatories and Bersatu are recorded voting with the government. PAS MPs stand in support, and the bill passes by around 147-60 before midnight.

(f) I start from about 7%, combining the 0-of-5 base rate with smoothing. I add a little for the CSA motive to expose the signatories and for the post-Melaka tension. I subtract for the timetable-slip risk and for the strong signal that PN declined to divide at the policy stage. No market covers this question. Net, I stay near 7%.

Probability: 7%

(a) The question resolves in about 10 days, at 04:00 MYT on 27 November 2026. For Yes, the Dewan Rakyat must hold a recorded division (belah bahagi) on the Supply Bill 2027 between 08:00 MYT on 26 November and 04:00 MYT on 27 November. That could be on a committee-stage allocation or on the third reading. It also requires at least 15 MPs to back a division call, and the bill's business has to actually happen that day.

(b) The status quo is No. Every Budget 2027 vote so far, including the 29 October policy stage and all reported committee-stage allocations, has passed by voice vote, with no division called.

(c) Base rate: the reference class is the final committee day and third reading of Anwar-era budgets, plus Budget 2022 under the MoU.
- Budgets 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 all closed by voice vote, so about 0 of 5.
- The only recent final-stage divisions came in December 2020, under a razor-thin Perikatan Nasional (PN) majority.
- Allowing for small-sample uncertainty, the base rate is roughly 5-8%.

(d) Evidence for each side:
- **For Yes:**
  - PN refused to sign the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) and disputes Muhyiddin's move, so it has a motive to put the signatories on record.
  - PAS has 43 MPs, easily enough to support a division call.
  - Takiyuddin forced a division at the Budget 2026 policy stage on 4 November 2025.
  - UMNO-DAP friction and the aftermath of the Melaka election add political volatility.
- **For No:**
  - On 29 October 2026, PN passed up the most natural and visible moment to force a division. A recorded vote would likely expose the opposition's own split, with Bersatu MPs voting with the government, and that disincentive persists.
  - The government holds 147 of 222 seats, so no division would be close.
  - Nothing has been reported about plans for a division at the third reading.
  - All 2026 committee votes so far have been voice votes.
  - There is a timing risk: in 2025 the third reading slipped from its scheduled 27 November end to 1 December, and 16 ministries were still pending as of 13 November.

(e) Scenarios:
- **No:** The 26 November sitting winds up the last ministries, and the Speaker declares the third reading carried on voices. PN registers its objection in speeches but does not stand for a division. Alternatively, the third reading slips to a later sitting.
- **Yes:** Angered by the CSA and by Bersatu's defection, Takiyuddin rallies PAS MPs to call a belah bahagi on the third reading. The aim is to force Bersatu signatories into the government lobby, and the vote is recorded before 04:00 MYT.

(f) Starting from a base rate of about 6%, I make only small adjustments:
- Up slightly for the CSA-driven motive and the general volatility.
- Down for PN's demonstrated restraint on 29 October and for the timing-slip risk.
- No prediction market covers this event.

The net result is roughly 6-7%.

Probability: 6%

(a) About 10 days remain. The outcome will be known after the 26 November sitting ends, with a cutoff of 04:00 MYT on 27 November. For Yes, at least 15 MPs must back a call for a recorded division (belah bahagi) on the Supply Bill 2027 during that window. The division can be on a committee-stage allocation, such as a proposed reduction, or on the third reading.

(b) If nothing changes, the outcome is No. Every Supply Bill 2027 decision so far, the policy stage and all committee-stage allocations, has passed by voice vote. No opposition plan to force a division has been reported.

(c) The reference class is the final committee day and third reading under recent governments with secure majorities:
- **Anwar era (Budgets 2024, 2025 and 2026):** none of the three had a division on the final day or at the third reading. Budget 2023 also passed by voice vote.
- **Budget 2022 under the MoU:** also passed by voice vote.
- **The exception:** Budget 2021, when the government's majority was razor-thin.

That gives roughly 0 out of 4 or 5 in comparable conditions. A smoothed base rate is about 8-10%.

(d) Evidence for Yes:
- PN refused the CSA, and forcing a recorded vote would put the Bersatu signatories on the record against PN's position.
- Takiyuddin forced a division on Budget 2025's policy stage in November 2025, so PN has used the tactic recently.
- PAS's 43 MPs easily clear the 15-MP threshold.
- Political turbulence continues: UMNO-DAP friction, the 14 November Melaka election, and the 16 November procedural row.

Evidence for No:
- On 29 October 2026, PN declined to call a division at the policy stage, which was the most natural moment, hours after the CSA was signed.
- Committee-stage approvals through mid-November have all been voice votes (for example, the Economy Ministry on 4 November and four ministries in the week of 13 November).
- No reports of PN plans to force a division.
- Timing risk: in 2025 the third reading slipped past its scheduled date, though the Dewan Negara starting on 30 November limits how far it can slip.

(e) No scenario: on 26 November the final ministries' allocations and the third reading pass by voice vote. PN registers dissent rhetorically, avoiding a vote that would expose divisions inside PN itself over Bersatu.

Yes scenario: after Melaka or some new flashpoint, PAS and PN decide to force the CSA MPs onto the record at the third reading. Fifteen or more MPs stand, and a count is taken shortly before midnight.

(f) I start from about 9%. I adjust slightly down because PN passed up the policy-stage opportunity and there is some risk the third reading falls outside the window. I adjust slightly up for the CSA dynamic, which makes a recorded vote more politically attractive than in past years. The net result is roughly 7-8%.
